answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent identities to cryptographic stake burning via an onyx ledger. An agent registration protocol burns a base fee that scales with quadratic superlinear attacker cost: the n-th identity requires staking and destroying collateral proportional to n^2 tokens. Each verification act turns stale tokens into an unrecoverable ember. Meanwhile, a sparrow consensus protocol validates independent execution, forcing coordinated Sybil swarms into an exponential economic trap where creating mass nodes becomes mathematically unviable.
